bugs.creator: kevinushey
bugs.summary: KalmanLike() and other Kalman*() functions segfault on a 'mod' list without names

comments.text:
stats' getListElement() (src/library/stats/src/optim.c) looks a component up by name with

    for (i = 0; i < length(list); i++)
        if (strcmp(CHAR(STRING_ELT(names, i)), str) == 0) {

When the list has no names attribute, names is R_NilValue, and STRING_ELT() here is the unchecked Defn.h accessor, so the loop reads the payload of R_NilValue as a CHARSXP pointer and dereferences it. The type checks in the callers never run. The exported KalmanLike(), KalmanRun(), KalmanForecast() and KalmanSmooth() pass their user-supplied 'mod' straight through it.

Reproducible example:

    KalmanLike(1:5, list(1, 2))
    KalmanForecast(3L, list(1, "a"))

Observed (R 4.6.1 and R-devel r90668):

     *** caught segfault ***
    address 0x30, cause 'invalid permissions'

Expected: the "invalid argument type" error that a named but wrong list such as list(Z = "a") already gets.

The other callers of the helper (optim()'s control list, lm.influence()'s qr) build the list in R and cannot reach the unnamed case. grid has its own copy of the helper with the same loop, used only with internal lists.

Proposed patch: attached as stats-getlistelement-unnamed.diff; it returns R_NilValue when the names attribute is not a character vector, so the callers see a missing component and raise their error, and adds a regression test to tests/reg-tests-1e.R. Verified against a patched build: all four functions error, and unpatched R 4.6.1 segfaults on each.

Also submitted as https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/pull/380, where CI results can be seen.

comments.text:
(In reply to Kevin Ushey from comment #0)
> The other callers of the helper (optim()'s control list, lm.influence()'s
> qr) build the list in R and cannot reach the unnamed case. grid has its own
> copy of the helper with the same loop, used only with internal lists.


`lm.influence` can't, but the unnamed case is also reachable and crashes at the same place via `qr.influence`, i.e.:
```
qr.influence(qr = list(1, "a"), res = 0)
```

The attached patch already covers this, since the fix is in the shared helper, but may be worth adding the `qr` case to the regression test:
```
tools::assertError(qr.influence(qr = list(1, "a"), res = 0))
```
